mainTopic: Do split coverings (שומר) join with a food for טומאה, and does a hair count as a handle (יד) or a covering?
overview: The גמרא asks whether two שומרין (protective coverings) can join with a food to reach the כביצה needed for טומאה. It shows from רבי יהודה's onion-peel משנה that there is no שומר on top of a שומר, so רב אושעיא must be asking about one covering split into pieces. Two proofs are brought, from legume pods and from grain sown in its shell. Both are pushed away: the pods case is about the stalk as a יד (handle), and the grain case is about grains on one stem that guard each other, or even one huge grain like the wheat of שמעון בן שטח's days. Next the גמרא goes back to the תוספתא about two bones carrying half-olives of corpse flesh whose ends were put into a house. ריש לקיש says only a bone counts as a יד, not a hair, while רבי יוחנן says even a hair counts. רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a משנה about a hide with flesh on it. The גמרא answers either that the hair is a שומר that pierces the hide (which raises a question about writing תפילין), or that it is a hair among many hairs, like רבי אלעא's awn among awns. A second version of the debate follows, and a further version begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Do two protective coverings combine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether two שומרין can join together with a food to make up the size needed for טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law: do two protective coverings join together?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question: can two protective coverings (שומרין) count together with the food toward the size needed for it to become טמא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that one שומר, like a peel or shell, counts together with the food toward the כביצה size. The new question is whether a second שומר can also count. The גמרא does not answer yet. First it will try to figure out what case this question is about.

keyTerms.meaning: Protective coverings of a food, like peels or shells. They protect the food and can count with it for טומאה.
"What is it?" The standard way to open a question about the law.
That they join together, meaning they combine to reach a required size.

phrases.english: Two protective coverings, what is the law about their joining together?
phrases.notes: "Joining together" means counting with the food to reach the egg-size needed for it to become טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule already known in the sugya that a single שומר joins with food for the טומאה size.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether two שומרין, and not just one, can count with the food toward the כביצה needed for טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: What case is the question about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the question means. It suggests a covering on top of another covering, then doubts that such a thing counts as a שומר at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say it is one covering on top of the other, is there such a thing as a covering on top of a covering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case the question is talking about. It tries the obvious picture, two layers one on top of the other, and immediately pushes back on it. This sets up a proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simplest picture of "two coverings" is two layers, an inner one and an outer one. But the גמרא doubts that an outer layer counts as a שומר at all, because it protects another covering and not the food itself. If that is so, the question has no case to apply to.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is it like?" The גמרא asks for the exact case being discussed.
"If you say." Introduces a suggested reading that the גמרא is about to reject.
One on top of the other, meaning layered.
"Is there such a thing?" A question that hints the answer is no.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say it is where this one is on top of that one,
phrases.notes: He means a food with two layers of covering, an outer one around an inner one.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִיכָּא שׁוֹמֵר עַל גַּב שׁוֹמֵר?
phrases.english: Is there such a thing as a protective covering on top of a protective covering?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא בְּזֶה עַל גַּב זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case the question from step 1 means, and challenges the most obvious answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical case "two שומרין" refers to.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the question is about two layers of covering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An outer layer protects only the inner covering, not the food, so it may not count as a שומר at all.

steps.title: Challenge from the three peels of an onion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה in a משנה: the inner onion peel always counts, the middle peel counts only when whole, and the outer peel never counts. So there is no שומר on top of a שומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: רבי יהודה says there are three peels on an onion. The inner one, whether whole or punctured, joins together. The middle one joins if it is whole, but not if it is punctured. The outer one is טהורה either way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove its doubt from the last step: a covering on top of another covering does not count as a שומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner peel counts as part of the food itself, so it always joins. The middle peel is the real שומר, so it joins only when whole and actually protecting. The outer peel sits on top of the middle שומר and never joins, which shows a second outer layer is not a שומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Peels or layers of skin.
Punctured or pierced, so it no longer fully protects.
Inner, middle, outer.
Pure. Here it means the peel does not join with the food for טומאה at all.

steps.confusionAlert: The inner peel joins even when punctured, not because it is a good שומר, but because it is treated like the food itself. The middle peel is the actual שומר, which is why its being whole matters.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in עוקצין.

phrases.english: There are three peels on an onion:

phrases.aramaic: פְּנִימִית, בֵּין שְׁלֵמָה בֵּין קְדוּרָה – מִצְטָרֶפֶת;
phrases.english: The inner one, whether whole or punctured, joins together;
the middle one, when whole, joins together,
when punctured, it does not join together;

phrases.aramaic: חִיצוֹנָה, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ – טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.english: the outer one, either way, is pure.
phrases.notes: "Either way" means whether it is whole or punctured.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שָׁלֹשׁ קְלִיפּוֹת בְּבָצָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the doubt raised in step 2 that a שומר on top of a שומר does not count.
steps.raayaObject: That there is no שומר on top of a שומר, so the question cannot be about two layers.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in עוקצין where רבי יהודה rules that the outer onion peel never joins.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the question as two layered coverings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the outer layer never counts, then asking whether two layered שומרין combine makes no sense.

steps.title: The real question: one covering split into pieces
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב אושעיא was asking about a single covering of the food that was divided into separate pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא was asking about a covering of food that someone divided.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true case behind the question. It is not two layers but one covering that was split into parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a layer on top of a layer never counts, "two שומרין" must mean something else. Here the food stays whole, but its single covering is cut into separate sections. The question is whether these sections still count together with the food, as if they were one שומר.

keyTerms.meaning: The protective covering of a food.
That one divided it into separate pieces.
"He is asking about." Identifies the real subject of a question.

steps.whatToRemember: There is no שומר on top of a שומר (proven from the onion peels). So the question of "two שומרין" is really about one covering divided into pieces around a whole food.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya, about a covering of food that one divided,
phrases.notes: The food itself stays whole. Only its covering is cut into separate sections.

phrases.english: is the one he is asking about.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא, שׁוֹמֵר אוֹכֶל שֶׁחִלְּקוֹ קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from steps 2 and 3 by giving a different case for the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question is about one שומר that was divided into separate pieces, not two layered שומרין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case of the question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question seemed to be about two layers of covering.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about one covering split into sections around a whole food.

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out both ways to think about a covering split into pieces. Each piece guards only its own part of the food, so maybe they don't join. Or since each piece does guard its own part, maybe they do join.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since this piece does not protect that part, and that piece does not protect this part, maybe they do not join. Or maybe, since this piece protects its own part and that piece protects its own part, they do join.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two possible ways of looking at רב אושעיא's question, so we can see exactly what is in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one looks at the pieces against each other: neither piece guards the other's food, so they are like two unrelated coverings. Side two looks at each piece on its own: every piece is a real שומר for its own food, so together they count as one covering of one food.

keyTerms.meaning: Protects or guards (the food)
They join together (to make up the needed size)
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

phrases.english: Since this one does not protect that one,
phrases.notes: "This one" is one piece of the covering, and "that one" is the part of the food under the other piece.

phrases.english: and that one does not protect this one,
it does not join together.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּהַאי מַגֵּין אַדִּידֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Or perhaps, since this one protects its own part,
and that one protects its own part, they join together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that step 4 defined the case as one covering split into pieces, this step lays out the two sides of the doubt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do separate pieces of one covering, each guarding only its own part of the food, join together for the size needed for טומאה?

steps.title: A proof from bean and legume pods
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who says that pods of legumes do become טמא because a person wants the pods while handling the legumes. A single pod is too small, so the pods seem to be joining together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה rules that the pod of beans is טהור, and the pod of legumes is טמא, because a person wants them when handling them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question with a ruling of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה about pods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A legume pod protects the legumes inside, so it is a שומר. One pod with its legumes is smaller than the size needed for טומאה, so if it becomes טמא, many separate pods must be joining together. That would show that separate pieces of covering do join.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules it pure (טהור)
Rules it impure (טמא)
A type of bean
Legumes (small beans or peas)
When handling them

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: Come and hear: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
rules pure in the case of a bean,
phrases.notes: He means the pod of a bean that touched something טמא.

phrases.english: and rules impure in the case of legumes,
because he wants them when handling them.
phrases.notes: A person wants to keep the pods so the legumes don't get damaged while he handles them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה מְטַהֵר בְּשֶׁל פּוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question that step 5 laid out.
steps.raayaObject: That separate pieces of covering join together to make up the size needed for טומאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's ruling that legume pods become טמא, even though one pod is smaller than the needed size

steps.title: The pods ruling is about the stalk as a handle
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא rejects the proof. The case is where the טומאה touched the stalk, and the stalk counts as a handle (יד), not a covering. "Handling them" means using the stalk to carry the legumes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said: It is about the stalk, and it is because of the rule of a handle. And what does "when handling them" mean? When using them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא pushes away the proof by saying the משנה is not talking about the pods as coverings at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the טומאה touched the stalk, the משנה is teaching the law of a handle (יד), which passes טומאה to the food it is attached to. So the ruling says nothing about separate coverings joining together, and the question stays open. The word "handling" is read as "using," meaning carrying the legumes by their stalk.

keyTerms.meaning: The stalk that the pods grow on
A handle; a part used to hold the food, with its own rules for טומאה
Their use (carrying them)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up שומר and יד. A שומר is a covering that protects the food, like a peel or pod. A יד is a handle used to hold the food, like a stalk. They are two separate categories.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the pods is rejected, because that case is about a handle (יד), not a covering (שומר). So we still don't know if a split covering joins together.

phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said:
It is about the stalk, and it is because of a handle,
And what does "when handling them" mean? When using them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: בְּקוּלְחָא, וּמִשּׁוּם יָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely by moving the case to a different category of law
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה was about pods as coverings (שומר). It is really about the stalk as a handle (יד), so it says nothing about coverings joining together.

steps.title: A proof from grain sown in its shell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the school of רבי ישמעאל: seed counts for טומאה the way people take it out to sow, meaning wheat, barley and lentils in their shells. Many small shells seem to join together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: the פסוק says 'on any sowing seed (that is sown)'. This means the seed counts the way people take it out for sowing: wheat in its shell, barley in its shell, and lentils in their shells.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again to answer רב אושעיא's question. It brings a teaching that says grain counts together with its shell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One grain plus its shell is far smaller than the size needed for טומאה. So if the shells count, it must be many grains and many separate shells added together. That would show that a covering split into pieces does join.

keyTerms.meaning: Seed that is sown. The words of the פסוק about food becoming טמא.
For sowing, planting in the field.
Shell or peel around the grain.
Lentils.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"On any sowing seed (that is sown)":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:37. Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: in the way that people take it out for sowing:
wheat in its shell, and barley in its shell,
and lentils in their shells.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from pods was rejected in step 7, the גמרא brings a new proof for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That separate pieces of a covering join together to make up the size for טומאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל on the פסוק 'זרע זרוע': grain counts in its shell, the way it is taken out for sowing.

steps.title: Rejection: the grains are on one stem and guard each other
steps.stepSummary: Just as רב אחא בריה דרבא explained the pods case as a stalk that acts as a handle, here the case is grains on one central stem, and the shells count as a covering for all of them together.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רב אחא בריה דרבא said: the case is about the stalk, and it counts as a handle. Here too, the case is about the central stem, and the shells count as a covering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from grain shells, using the same kind of answer רב אחא בריה דרבא gave for the pods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is grains still attached around one stem. There, if one grain with its shell falls off, the others fall too, so each shell helps protect all the grains. That is different from רב אושעיא's case, where each piece guards only its own part of the food, so there is no proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Stalk, the stem the pods hang on.
Handle, a part used to hold the food. It passes טומאה to and from the food, but it does not count toward the food's size.
Literally a spine. Here, the central stem of the ear that the grains are attached to.
Here too. Using the same answer for a new case.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two answers. In the pods case the stalk is a יד (handle). In the grain case the stem is about שומר (covering), because the shells guard each other.

phrases.english: As Rav Acha son of Rava said,
phrases.notes: This points back to his answer about the pods in step 7.

phrases.english: it is about the stalk, and it counts because it is a handle.
Here too, it is about the central stem, and it counts because it is a covering.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא, בְּקוּלְחָא, וּמִשּׁוּם יָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 8 by placing the case on grains still attached to a stem.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof. רב אושעיא's question is still open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed loose grains, each with its own shell. But the case is grains on one stem, where every shell guards all the grains, not just its own part.

steps.title: Why would the lower grains need the upper ones?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that all the grains guard each other. The upper grains rest on the lower ones, but the lower ones don't seem to depend on the upper ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the upper grains need the lower ones. But why would the lower grains need the upper ones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 9. It questions whether the shells really guard each other in both directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a lower grain falls, the grains above lose their support. But if an upper grain falls, the lower ones still seem to stay in place. So the upper shells would not be guarding the lower grains, and the idea that every shell guards all the grains seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense. Opens a challenge: one side is fine, but the other is a problem.
The upper ones, the grains higher on the stem.
The lower ones, the grains lower on the stem.
They need, they depend on.

phrases.english: Granted, the upper ones need the lower ones,
but the lower ones, why do they need the upper ones?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא עִילִּיָּתָא צְרִיכִי לְתַתָּיָתָא, אֶלָּא תְּתַּיָּתָא מַאי צְרִיכִי לְעִילִּיָּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 9 that all the shells on the stem guard each other.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 9 that every shell on the stem guards all the grains.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The support only goes one way. Lower grains hold up upper ones, but upper grains don't seem to hold up lower ones.

steps.title: The grains sit tightly in one row
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the grains are packed tightly around the stem in one row, so if even an upper one falls, the rest come loose too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where they are in a single row.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 10 in two words: the grains are in one tight row.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the grains are packed tightly together, each one holds the others in place. Then losing an upper grain also loosens the lower ones, so every shell really does guard all the grains. That keeps the rejection of step 9 standing.

keyTerms.meaning: In one row, packed closely together.
A row or a layer.
One.

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from grain shells fails. The shells on one stem all guard each other, which is not like רב אושעיא's case of pieces that each guard only their own part. So far his question is still not answered.

phrases.english: It is where they are in a single row.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 and keeps the rejection of step 9 in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the grains are packed tightly in one row.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lower grains do not depend on the upper ones, so the upper shells do not guard them.
steps.terutzMaskana: In one tight row, every grain holds the others in place, so all the shells guard all the grains.

steps.title: Can one row of grain reach the size of an egg?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer. Can one row of grains packed around a stem really add up to a כביצה of food?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really an egg's worth of food in a single row of grain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes at the answer from step 11. One row of small grains seems far too little to reach the size of an egg (כביצה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 explained that the grains in one tight row around the stem act as one unit, so the shells guard all of them together. But for this food to matter for טומאה, it needs to reach a כביצה. A single row of ordinary wheat grains doesn't seem to come anywhere near that amount.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of an egg, the amount of food that matters for טומאה
Food
A row or layer (here, of grains)

phrases.english: And is there an egg-bulk
of food in one row?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא כְּבֵיצָה אֳכָלִין בְּחַד דָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practical possibility of the case described in step 11's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 11 that one tightly packed row of grains is treated as a unit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single row of normal grains is too small to make up the egg-bulk needed for food to matter for טומאה, so the case seems impossible.

steps.title: The huge wheat of שמעון בן שטח's days
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the case is talking about the huge wheat grains from the time of שמעון בן שטח. With grains that big, one row can easily reach a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about wheat like the wheat in the days of שמעון בן שטח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case is about very large grains, like the wheat in the days of שמעון בן שטח. With grains that size, one row can hold an egg's worth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was about the amount of food, not about the rule itself. By pointing to grains of exceptional size, the גמרא shows the case can happen. So the explanation from step 11 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Wheat grains of

phrases.english: With wheat of the days of Shimon ben Shatach.
phrases.notes: In his time, grains grew famously huge, so a few of them could add up to a lot of food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to unusually large grains
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One row of grain is far too small to make up an egg-bulk, so the case could not happen.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is about extra-large wheat, like in the days of שמעון בן שטח, where one row does reach a כביצה.

steps.title: With grains that big, even one grain is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that once we are talking about the huge wheat of שמעון בן שטח's time, we don't need a whole row at all. Even one single grain could be the case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, even one grain of wheat works, if it is wheat like in the days of שמעון בן שטח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from its own answer. If a grain can be that big, the ברייתא could simply be talking about one grain in its shell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9 to 11 worked hard to show that many grains in one row guard each other. But if one huge grain can be a כביצה all by itself, that whole setup is no longer needed. The shell then simply covers that one grain.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this point
One grain of wheat

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about seed in shells can now be read simply: one huge grain, like those of שמעון בן שטח's time, guarded by its own shell. We no longer need the idea of many grains joining together.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not reject the idea that the shell counts. It only removes the need to explain how many grains guard each other.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
even one grain of wheat also works,
with wheat of the days of Shimon ben Shatach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer of step 13 and makes the explanation of steps 10-11 unnecessary.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא can be talking about a single huge grain in its shell. The shell guards it, and it reaches a כביצה on its own.

steps.title: Back to the תוספתא: two bones with half-olives of flesh
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the תוספתא quoted earlier. Two bones each carry half an olive-size piece of corpse flesh. Their bare ends are put into a house, and the house becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the text itself. Two bones each have half an olive-bulk of flesh on them. Someone put the ends of both bones into a house, and the house covers those ends. The house is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word גופא, the גמרא goes back to study the תוספתא it quoted earlier on 118b. It quotes the case of two bones whose ends were put into a house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each bone carries only half a כזית of corpse flesh, which alone is too little to spread טומאה. Only the bare ends of the bones are inside the house, not the flesh. Still, the house becomes טמא. That means the bones act like handles bringing the flesh's טומאה inside, and the two half-olives join together into one כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: The text itself: going back to examine a source quoted earlier
Bones
Halves of an olive-bulk
Covers or overhangs, so that טומאת אהל spreads
Ritually impure

steps.whyThisMatters: This case links back to the idea of a handle (יד) from step 7. Something attached to the טומאה can bring it into a place even when the טומאה itself stays outside.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to the תוספתא it quoted earlier, on 118b.

phrases.english: Two bones, and on them
are two halves of an olive-bulk,
phrases.notes: Half an olive's worth of corpse flesh sits on one end of each bone.

phrases.english: and he put the ends of both into a house,
phrases.notes: These are the other ends of the bones, without the flesh.

phrases.english: and the house covers them,
the house is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new section, going back to examine the תוספתא quoted earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two bones each carry half a כזית of corpse flesh and only their bare ends are inside a house, the house is טמא.

steps.title: יהודה בן נקוסא asks: how can two bones join?
steps.stepSummary: יהודה בן נקוסא, quoting רבי יעקב, questions the ruling. How can two separate bones join together to make one כזית?
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה בן נקוסא says in the name of רבי יעקב: How can two bones join together to make an olive-bulk?
steps.whatsHappening: The תוספתא continues with a different view. יהודה בן נקוסא, quoting רבי יעקב, doubts that two separate bones can add their half-olives together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said the house is טמא because the two half-olives join to make one כזית. יהודה בן נקוסא's objection is aimed only at this joining. Each bone has less than a כזית, so he asks how two separate bones could combine into one measure.

keyTerms.meaning: How?
Join together to make up a measure
An olive-bulk, the smallest amount of corpse flesh that spreads טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: His question is only about joining two separate half-olives. He does not argue with the idea that a bone can bring the flesh's טומאה into the house.

phrases.english: Yehuda ben Nekosa says
in the name of Rabbi Yaakov:
How can two bones
join together to make an olive-bulk?

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהוּדָה בֶּן נָקוֹסָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a disagreeing view within the same תוספתא, questioning step 15's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to יהודה בן נקוסא in the name of רבי יעקב, two separate bones each with half a כזית do not join to make a כזית.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: A bone counts as a handle, but a hair does not
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש limits the earlier ruling. Only a bone works as a 'handle' that brings the flesh's טומאה into the house. A hair does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: This ruling was taught only about a bone, because a bone counts as a handle. But a hair does not count as a handle.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש tells us the limits of the earlier case. The house becomes טמא through a bone attached to the flesh, but it would not become טמא through a hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'handle' (יד) is something attached to טמא material that passes the טומאה along, as if it were part of it. ריש לקיש holds that a bone is strong and important enough to be a handle, while a thin hair is not.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They taught this only...': a way of limiting a ruling to one specific case
Literally 'hand'. A handle: something attached to food or flesh that passes on its טומאה
Bone
A single hair

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
They taught this only about a bone,
because it counts as a handle,
but a hair does not count as a handle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא עֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the case of the bones and the house, and limits it to bones only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bone counts as a handle for the flesh attached to it. A hair does not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Even a hair counts as a handle
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with ריש לקיש. Even a hair counts as a handle, so a hair attached to flesh could also bring the טומאה into the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Even a hair also counts as a handle.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite opinion. A hair works as a handle just like a bone does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is a clear argument (מחלוקת). For ריש לקיש a hair is too weak to be a handle. For רבי יוחנן even a hair passes on the טומאה. This sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
Also

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Even a hair also counts as a handle.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ נִימָא נָמֵי הָוְיָא יָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to ריש לקיש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hair also counts as a handle for the flesh.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a hide with flesh on it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a משנה: if a hide has a כזית of flesh on it, a person who touches a hair on the other side of the hide is טמא. Isn't that because the hair is a handle?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: A hide with a כזית of flesh on it. One who touches a strand coming out of the flesh, or a hair on the opposite side, is טמא. Isn't the reason that it counts as a handle?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's view with a משנה. In that משנה, touching a hair makes a person טמא, which seems to show that a hair is a handle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person never touched the flesh itself, only a hair on the other side of the hide. The simplest reason he is still טמא is that the hair is a handle for the flesh. That goes against ריש לקיש, who said a hair is not a handle.

keyTerms.meaning: Hide (animal skin)
An olive's size, the smallest amount that passes on this טומאה
A thin strand or fiber of flesh
'Is it not...?': the גמרא suggests the obvious reason in order to make a challenge

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
A hide that has an olive's size of flesh on it,
phrases.notes: This is the hide of a נבלה, an animal that died without proper slaughter.

phrases.english: one who touches a strand coming out of it,
or a hair opposite it, is impure.
Is it not because it counts as a handle?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's position from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that a hair is not a handle
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that touching a hair attached to the hide makes one טמא, which seems to happen only if the hair counts as a handle.

steps.title: The hair counts as a protective covering, not a handle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש: the hair makes a person טמא because it is a שומר, a protective covering for the flesh, not because it is a handle.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is because the hair is a protective covering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The hair passes on טומאה for a different reason: it is a שומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר is something that covers and protects food, like a shell or peel, and it counts as part of the food for טומאה. So the משנה can be explained without saying a hair is a handle, and ריש לקיש's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective covering (like a peel or shell) that counts as part of the food for טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: Handle (יד) and protective covering (שומר) are two separate ways something can pass on טומאה. The answer here switches from one to the other.

phrases.english: No, it is because it is a protective covering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the משנה's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hair makes a person טמא because it is a handle.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hair makes a person טמא because it is a protective covering.

steps.title: Can there be a covering on top of a covering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the hide already protects the flesh, and the hair sits on top of the hide. Can a covering on top of another covering count as a שומר?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there such a thing as a covering on top of a covering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given. The hair seems to protect the hide, not the flesh itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hide is the real covering of the flesh. The hair is on the outside of the hide, so at most it is a second layer. The question is whether a second layer can still count as a שומר of the flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And is there...?': a question meaning that something should not be possible
On top of

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִיכָּא שׁוֹמֵר עַל גַּבֵּי שׁוֹמֵר?
phrases.english: But is there a protective covering on top of a protective covering?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא שׁוֹמֵר עַל גַּבֵּי שׁוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the hair is a שומר for the flesh
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The hair is outside the hide, which is already the covering, so it seems too far away from the flesh to protect it.

steps.title: The hair goes right through the hide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the hair pierces through the hide and reaches the flesh, so it protects the flesh directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: It goes all the way through.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the hair is not just sitting on top of the hide. It passes through the hide and touches the flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hair reaches the flesh directly, it is not a 'covering on a covering.' It is a direct covering of the flesh, so it counts as a שומר.

keyTerms.meaning: It pierces right through

phrases.english: It pierces right through.
phrases.notes: The hair goes all the way through the hide until it reaches the flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the facts of how hair sits in hide
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hair only sits on the outside of the hide.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hair goes through the hide and touches the flesh directly.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: Then how can we write תפילין?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב objects: if hairs go through the hide, then the hide is full of holes. תפילין need perfect writing with no holes, so how can they be written on such hide?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב objected: If so, how do we write תפילין? We need perfect writing, and there would not be any!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב attacks the last answer. If the hair goes through the hide, the hide must have tiny holes, and that causes a problem for writing תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters of תפילין must be complete, with no holes breaking them. If every hair hole goes all the way through the hide, the letters written on it would have holes in them. That would make kosher תפילין impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it: a strong challenge from a later sage
'But now (if so)...': introduces a problem that follows from the last idea
תפילין, written on parchment made from hide
Perfect, complete writing with no holes or breaks

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov objected to it:
But if that is so,
how do we write tefillin?
Don't we need perfect writing,
and there is none!
phrases.notes: Because the hair holes would go through the parchment and break the letters.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 22 by showing a problem it creates.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that hairs pierce all the way through the hide
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the hide has holes all the way through, writing on it could never be perfect, so תפילין could never be kosher.

steps.title: A hole that ink passes over is not a hole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רב אחא בר יעקב: he overlooked the rule from ארץ ישראל that a hole the ink can cover does not count as a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב forgot what they say in ארץ ישראל: any hole that the ink passes over is not considered a hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 23 about how תפילין can be written on hide full of tiny hair holes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא בר יעקב thought the hair holes would ruin the writing of תפילין. The answer: these holes are so tiny that ink flows right over them, and a hole like that does not count as a hole. So the idea that hair goes through the hide, from step 22, stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It slipped his mind; he overlooked it
In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
A hole
Ink

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule for סת"ם (writing ספרי תורה, תפילין and מזוזות): a tiny hole that the ink covers does not make the writing invalid.

phrases.english: He overlooked that which they say in the West:
phrases.notes: 'The West' is how the בבלי refers to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Any hole that the ink passes over
is not a hole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא בר יעקב's challenge from step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings in an overlooked rule that removes the problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hair holes would make the hide invalid for writing תפילין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Holes so small that ink covers them do not count as holes, so the writing is fine.

steps.title: Second answer: the hair is a handle when it is a hair among hairs
steps.stepSummary: Another way to answer רבי יוחנן: the whole משנה is about a יד, and the hair counts as a handle only when many hairs are held together, like רבי אלעא's 'awn among awns'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: the whole משנה works because of 'handle'. As רבי אלעא said, it is talking about an awn among many awns. Here too, it is talking about a hair among many hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to רבי יוחנן's challenge from step 19, without using the idea of שומר at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the גמרא agrees that the hair in the משנה counts as a יד. But ריש לקיש only said that one single hair is too weak to be a handle. When many hairs are held together, you can lift the flesh by them, so they act as a handle, and ריש לקיש is not contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces another answer
A handle: a part that lets you hold or lift the food
An awn: the thin bristle sticking out from the top of a grain stalk
A hair

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say ריש לקיש was wrong. He spoke about a single hair. This answer is about many hairs together, which are strong enough to be a handle.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
the whole thing is because of 'handle',
phrases.notes: He means the whole משנה from step 19: both the flesh strand and the hair make you טמא as handles.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Ela said:
It is talking about an awn among the awns.
Here too, it is talking about a hair among the hairs.
phrases.notes: Many hairs held together are strong enough to lift the flesh, so they work like a handle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to רבי יוחנן's challenge in step 19, instead of the שומר answer of steps 20 to 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (many hairs, not one)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows that a hair is a handle, against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about many hairs together, which do work as a handle. ריש לקיש was only talking about a single hair.

steps.title: Where did רבי אלעא say his rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי אלעא's statement about 'an awn among awns' was originally said.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where was רבי אלעא's statement said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move: it wants to show the original place of רבי אלעא's rule that it just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 quoted רבי אלעא but did not say what he was explaining. Now the גמרא goes to find the original משנה so we can see his rule in its home setting.

keyTerms.meaning: And where was it said?

phrases.english: And where was the statement of Rabbi Ela said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the statement quoted in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The original context of רבי אלעא's 'awn among awns' rule.

steps.title: The משנה about awns on grain stalks
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעא said his rule about a משנה teaching that awns on grain stalks can become טמא and make other things טמא, but do not join together with the food for the required amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said about this משנה: the awns on the stalks become טמא and make other things טמא, but they do not join together with the food to make up the needed amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by quoting the משנה that רבי אלעא was explaining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה treats the awn as a יד: like a handle, it can carry טומאה to and from the food. But it is not food itself, so it does not count toward the size needed to give טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain stalks or ears of grain
They become טמא and make other things טמא
Join together to reach the required size

phrases.english: On this: the awn that is on the stalks
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in עוקצין 1:3.

phrases.english: become impure and make things impure,
but they do not join together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26 by quoting the source משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעא's statement was said on the משנה about awns on grain stalks.

steps.title: What use is a thin awn as a handle?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what an awn is good for: it is so thin, how can it count as a handle for the stalk?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is an awn good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the משנה: a single awn is too weak to lift anything, so how can it be a handle?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יד must be something you can actually hold and lift the food with. One thin bristle would just snap off, so it seems it should not count as a handle at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it fit for? What use is it?

phrases.english: An awn, what is it good for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the משנה just quoted in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a thin, weak awn can work as a handle.

steps.title: רבי אלעא: an awn among many awns
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעא answers that the משנה is talking about many awns together, which are strong enough to act as a handle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעאי said: the משנה is talking about an awn among many awns.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is רבי אלעא's original statement: the משנה is talking about a bunch of awns, not one alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many awns held together can lift the stalk without breaking off, so together they work as a handle. This is the same idea step 25 used for many hairs on the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: An awn among many awns: a group of bristles held together

steps.whatToRemember: A single thin thing (one awn, one hair) is too weak to be a יד. But many of them together can lift the food, so they count as a handle. This is how the second answer saves ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ilai said:
phrases.notes: This is the same רבי אלעא from step 25, just spelled a little differently.

phrases.english: It is talking about an awn among the awns.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעַאי: בִּמְלַאי שֶׁבֵּין הַמְּלָאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28 and shows the source of the rule used in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה means many awns together, which can work as a handle.

steps.title: Introducing another version of the debate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that some people tell the whole discussion in a different way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it in another version.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second version of the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about hair. The next steps show how this version goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled yet; this line only opens a new telling of the same debate. In this version, the discussion focuses on whether the hair works as a שומר or as a יד.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version: a different telling of the same discussion

phrases.english: Some say it in another version.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the hair debate between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, which the first version worked through in steps 17 to 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A second version of the hair discussion is about to be given.

steps.title: Hair makes sense only as protection, not as a handle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the view that hair counts as a שומר, because one single hair seems useless as a handle.
steps.simpleTranslation: It also makes sense that the reason is that hair is a protection. If you think the reason is that hair is a handle, what is one hair good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a logical support for saying that touching the hair makes a person טמא because the hair is a שומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A handle has to be strong enough to lift or hold the thing it is attached to. One thin hair cannot do that, so calling it a יד seems wrong. A protection does not need strength, so שומר fits better.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense: a logical support for a view
Protection: a part that guards the food, like a peel or shell
Handle: a part used to hold the food
A single hair

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up שומר and יד. A שומר guards the food. A יד is something you hold the food by. The question here is which one hair counts as.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
that it is because of protection,
for if it enters your mind that it is because of a handle –
for what is one hair fit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first argument inside the second version.
steps.raayaObject: The view that hair counts as a שומר and not as a יד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: one single hair is too weak to serve as a handle.

steps.title: One hair among many hairs can be a handle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the case is a hair among many hairs, just as רבי אלעא explained 'an awn among awns'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אלעא said: it is talking about an awn among the awns. Here too, it is talking about a hair among the hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 31. Hair can count as a handle when there are many hairs together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof said one hair is too weak to be a יד. The answer is that the case is not one lone hair but a hair that is part of a bunch. Many hairs together are strong enough to work as a handle. This is the same idea רבי אלעא used for awns on grain.

keyTerms.meaning: Awn: the thin, bristly hair on top of a grain stalk
Among the hairs: one hair that is part of a group

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ela said:
with regard to an awn among the awns,
here too – with regard to a hair among the hairs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the logical support given in step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects the idea that hair cannot be a יד. It does not deny that a single lone hair is weak.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof pictured one lone hair, but the case is a hair together with many other hairs.

steps.title: Where was רבי אלעא's rule first said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי אלעא's rule about awns was originally stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where was the statement of רבי אלעאי said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the original place of רבי אלעא's rule. This is the same question it asked in the first version, now repeated as part of this version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To use a rule properly, we need to know its original setting. The next step points to the משנה where רבי אלעא first said it.

keyTerms.meaning: Where was it said? A question asking for the original setting of a statement

phrases.english: And where was that of Rabbi Ilai stated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule just used in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The original context of רבי אלעא's 'awn among awns' rule.

steps.title: The משנה about awns on grain stalks
steps.stepSummary: The rule was said about a משנה that awns on stalks become טמא and spread טומאה, but do not join to make the required amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: On what we learned in a משנה: Awns that are on the stalks become טמא and make other things טמא, but they do not join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the משנה where רבי אלעא's rule was said: awns on grain stalks can become טמא and make other things טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Awns can become טמא and pass on טומאה because they count as a handle for the grain. But they do not add to the size of the food when we measure whether there is enough food to make something טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain stalks or ears of grain
They become טמא and make other things טמא
They join together with the food to make up the required size

phrases.english: On that which we learned in a mishna:
The awns that are on the stalks
become impure and make impure
but do not join together.
phrases.notes: Meaning they do not add to the food to reach the minimum size needed to make something טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 33 by naming the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule was said on the משנה about awns on grain stalks.

steps.title: What is a thin awn good for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how something as thin as an awn can count as a handle for the stalk.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is an awn good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the משנה. An awn is so thin, so how can it act as a handle that becomes טמא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same problem raised about one single hair. Something too weak to hold the stalk should not count as a יד. The next step gives רבי אלעא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it good for? Asks what use or function something has

phrases.english: For what is an awn fit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the משנה just quoted in step 34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How an awn, which is so thin, can work as a handle for the stalk.

steps.title: רבי אלעא: an awn among many awns
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעא answers that the משנה means an awn that is part of a bunch of awns, which together are strong enough to be a handle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעאי said: It is talking about an awn among the awns.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעא explains that the משנה is not talking about one lone awn but an awn among many awns, which together can work as a handle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the original source of the rule used in step 32. Many thin things together can be strong enough to hold, so they count as a יד. That is why the same idea works for a hair among many hairs.

keyTerms.meaning: Among the awns: one awn that is part of a group

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the answer is the same: one weak strand alone is not a handle, but one strand among many strands can be. This works for awns on grain and for hair on a hide.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one sage's rule from a totally different topic, grain stalks, is used to answer a question about hair on meat.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ilai said:
With regard to an awn among the awns.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעַאי: בִּמְלַאי שֶׁבֵּין הַמְּלָאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is talking about many awns together, which are strong enough to act as a handle.

steps.title: Some teach the dispute differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that there is another version of the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are those who teach it in a different way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It tells us that some people taught the earlier argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש in a different way, and that version is about to be presented.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is proven or challenged here yet. This line opens yet another version of the dispute. It comes after the first version and the לישנא אחרינא of step 30. The learner should expect the same two אמוראים, but with the argument stated or placed differently.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach (it): introduces a second version of a teaching or dispute
Teach or recite a tradition. Here it means passing down the dispute in a certain form.
It: points back to the dispute already discussed

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument with new people. It is the same dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, just handed down in a different form.

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it
phrases.notes: "It" means the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש from earlier. A different way of teaching it is about to come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the לישנא אחרינא (steps 30-36), the גמרא introduces yet another version of the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is an alternative tradition of how the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש was taught. Its content continues on the next amud.
